title: Unconfirmed observation: the dashboard `dateRange` "Custom…" option did not open a picker under automation — needs a re-drive on a current console build before it is treated as a defect
body:
## Symptom

> **Read this first: this is an unconfirmed observation, not a reproduced defect.** The dashboards run deliberately did **not** file it as a bug — it was recorded as something to re-check, and this card exists only so the re-check is not lost. Nothing here asserts broken behaviour.

While driving the dashboards area, selecting **"Custom…"** in a `dateRange` global filter did not appear to open a date-range picker under browser automation. Expected: the custom-range picker opens and accepts an explicit start/end window.

What makes it weak evidence, stated plainly:

- observed under automation only, with no manual confirmation;
- not reproduced, and no repeat-count recorded;
- the console under test was the **vendored** build (`09987b68`), which is many commits behind objectui `origin/main` — in the same run the vendored pin was found to trail `origin/main` by 138 commits;
- a picker that fails to open under automation is a classic driver/timing artifact (portal-rendered popovers, animation settling), which is exactly why the run declined to call it.

The rest of the `dateRange` surface behaved (the dashboards run's global-filter and drill-through items passed, including half-open month bounds on drill).

## Root cause

**Not located by the run.** No source was inspected for this observation, and no failing selector or console error was captured.

## Reproduction

Not established — establishing it *is* the work. Required next step:

1. Re-drive the "Custom…" option of a `dateRange` global filter against a **current console build** (objectui `origin/main`, not the vendored `09987b68` pin), in a fresh browser session.
2. Drive it manually as well as under automation, so a driver artifact can be told apart from a real failure.
3. **If it reproduces on a current build**, it becomes a real defect and the card belongs in **objectui** (console date-range filter control) with the captured evidence — this card is not that card.
4. **If it does not reproduce**, close this as an automation artifact and note it, so the next run does not re-litigate it.

No `domain:*` lane is applied: there is nothing to fix in this repo unless step 3 lands, and if it does, the fix is cross-repo in objectui.

## Source

Extracted from the QA run objectstack-ai/objectstack#7515 (framework a86db175).
